lines: In this short wrap-up from New York, Nicolai Tangen and Marthe Skaar revisit his Mike Milken interview, framing Milken's high-yield career as a lesson in questioning what markets label 'safe'.

They note high-yield debt funded riskier companies that banks ignored and helped consolidate industries such as telecom and media, while a diversified pool of 'risky' credits can deliver higher returns with lower aggregate volatility.

Tangen highlights Milken's method of changing minds with simple multiple-choice questions rather than confrontation, and stresses auditing positions daily by asking whether you would buy them again today.
They contrast US agility in absorbing losses and pivoting with slower, legacy-burdened recovery in Europe.
Tangen warns that firms failing to integrate AI face existential risk, as private equity buyers increasingly acquire legacy companies specifically to replace labor with automation.
podcast: In Good Company with Nicolai Tangen
title: Friday Wrap-Up: Milken’s Method and a Tech Day in New York
